purpose: Convert the decision memo, risk register, runbook, and evidence pack into a practical private GitHub repository execution checklist.

approved: Copy approved starter files and generated fixtures
Import labels, milestones, owner lanes, and first issue wave
Open the first PR with proof, rollback notes, and reviewer lanes
Capture exact GitHub Actions check names before branch protection
notApproved: No live payment keys or billing capture

executionGates: Product owner confirms the controlled go is for repo creation and first PR evidence only.
Repo is private before files, labels, issues, or screenshots are added.
No .env, live token, billing key, certificate, workbook, or customer file is in the copy set.
Labels, milestones, issue waves, and board columns are either imported or explicitly deferred.
Work starts on a branch with PR discipline; main is not used as a working branch.
Evidence folder exists before commands run so transcripts, screenshots, and notes have a home.
Branch protection waits until actual GitHub Actions check names appear.
Open blockers, placeholders, rollback note, and next owner are documented before merge.
executionSequence: Open the decision memo, state go/hold/no-go, and record the owner who can stop the session.
Create `dhirajnyse/pursuitdesk-platform` as private and capture visibility proof.
Clone locally, create the working branch, and keep main untouched.
Copy root docs, API shell, packages, workflow shells, env examples, scripts, and evidence folder.
Capture auth, install, quality, route, auth tenant, and release-gate proof or placeholder notes.
Create labels, milestones, owner lanes, and project board columns.
Open the first M0/M1 issues with proof commands and acceptance criteria.
Link issue, scope, risk register, evidence pack, rollback note, reviewers, and placeholders.
Workflow files need exact job and check names from the first Actions run.
Only after check names exist, configure required PR review and status checks.
Save screenshots, command transcripts, PR note, branch rules, and owner signoffs.
Record what passed, what was deferred, what blocks live SaaS, and who owns v129.
operatorChecklist: Controlled repo opening approved; live SaaS, live data, billing capture, and production hosting stay out of scope.
Visibility proof captured before adding files or issues.
No secrets, customer files, commercial values, invoices, certificates, or live keys in source folder.
Root docs, API shell, packages, scripts, workflow files, env examples, and evidence folder copied.
Labels, milestones, issue routing, proof labels, owner lanes, and project columns created.
Foundation, security, data, CI, billing, and release issues opened in the planned order.
Scope, linked issue, risk note, command proof, rollback note, and reviewer list included.
Secret and live-data scan documented before review.
Actual workflow check names copied into the evidence pack.
Required checks use actual names; conversation resolution and review rules are captured.
Placeholder commands, failed checks, missing secrets, and deferred work are explicit.
Go/hold/no-go status recorded for product, platform, backend, security, data, and QA.
stopRules: Do not upload files. Change visibility or recreate the repo privately, then capture evidence.
Remove it, rotate the credential, clean history if needed, and record the incident.
Remove workbook, restart from generated fixture-only data, and update proof notes.
Remove value, LOA, agreement, invoice, billing, and negotiation fields from operational examples.
Pause until the person with stop authority confirms go/hold/no-go.
Do not configure required status checks until the first Actions run exposes actual names.
Add rollback note, release impact, and evidence path before review.
Every first PR change must link to issue, owner, milestone, acceptance checks, and proof command.
proofLog: Repo settings or visibility area proving private status.
`gh auth status`, git version, node version, package manager, and local path notes.
Folder tree showing apps, packages, infra, docs, workflows, scripts, env examples, and evidence.
Manual scan results for secrets, workbooks, certificates, billing keys, and commercial fields.
Issue URLs, labels, milestones, owners, proof commands, and opening order.
PR link, title, scope, risk reference, command proof, rollback, and reviewer lanes.
Exact workflow names, job labels, check names, artifacts, and failure policy.
Required checks, review policy, admin bypass decision, conversation resolution, and release gate.
repoScreenPlan: Capture before first file upload or issue import.
Capture first branch file tree and evidence folder.
Capture labels grouped by scope, priority, security, proof, and release.
Capture filtered M0/M1 issue wave with owners and milestones.
Capture PR body, linked issue, reviewers, checks, and evidence references.
Capture workflow run summary and exact check names before branch protection.
Capture required status checks, review settings, and conversation resolution.
Capture opening columns, blocked items, and owner movement.
commandRunOrder: Confirm the GitHub account before repo execution.
Clone the private repo after visibility proof.
Create the working branch; main stays clean.
Install dependencies or record exact blocker if package shell is not yet executable.
Run quality proof once scripts exist; otherwise create issue-linked placeholder.
Run type proof once TS shell exists; otherwise attach placeholder and owner.
Run tenant/access proof when middleware is present.
Summarize proof, blockers, rollback, and owner decision.
issueWave: Root docs, workspace, scripts, environment examples, and evidence folder.
No secrets, tenant guard placeholder, commercial redaction, and denial audit expectations.
Health, auth, users, records, commercial vault, import, billing, feedback, and audit route shells.
Tenant seed, migration order, source trace, rollback, duplicate quarantine, and fixture assertions.
Workflow shells, artifact policy, release gate, exact check names, and branch protection.
USD plans, test-mode checkout, seat reconciliation, access locks, and billing audit events.
ownerBoard: Approves controlled repo day and confirms what is not approved.
Creates repo, branch, taxonomy, workflow proof, and branch protection evidence.
Owns starter files, package scripts, route shells, and first PR quality proof.
Owns no-secret rule, tenant guards, access checks, commercial redaction, and denial audit.
Owns generated data, migration sequence, source trace, rollback, and no-workbook rule.
Owns proof folder, screenshots, check names, branch rules, signoffs, and closeout.
branchTiming: Keep branch protection note in draft until first workflow run exists.
Capture workflow, job, and required status check names exactly as GitHub shows them.
CODEOWNERS or reviewer policy must match platform, backend, security, data, and QA lanes.
Require PR, required checks, conversation resolution, and review approval.
Document admin bypass policy and emergency merge owner.
Evidence folder, rollback note, open blockers, and owner signoffs are complete.
completionChecklist: Private repo evidence exists before any files moved.
File tree and first branch show only approved shell files and generated fixtures.
Generated issue bodies are ready; first wave URLs are recorded or explicitly deferred.
Proof command output or issue-linked placeholders are stored in evidence files.
Secret, customer file, workbook, and commercial-field scan is complete.
Scope, risk, proof, rollback, reviewers, and blocker notes are clear.
Required status checks use actual GitHub names, not guessed file names.
Passed, deferred, blocked, next owner, and v129 control board handoff are written.
handoff: v128 turns the decision memo, risk register, runbook, and evidence pack into a concrete private repo execution checklist.
The checklist is intentionally practical: gates, timeline, owners, proof logs, command order, issue wave, branch timing, stop rules, and completion checks.
The safest next real-world move is to run this checklist only when the private GitHub repo is ready, then capture proof before branch protection and first merge.
v129 can now turn execution into a live Backend Alpha Control Board for repo status, PR status, evidence, blockers, and owner signoff movement.
